raw_response:
I’m already old, so I don’t like to gamble much. With only 16.1 mu and just two people in the house, I have to keep things steady. Wheat and maize are still my main support because that rotation is familiar and safer. Stevia can make money if the buyer is good, but I won’t put too much land into it because it needs more care and labor. I’ll keep most land in the wheat-maize cycle and leave a smaller piece for stevia. Same as the farmers around me, I’ll use the well when the crop really needs water, but not too many times because pumping costs money. Fertilizer I will not cut too hard, because if the crop turns yellow or weak, yield drops fast and I cannot make that back.

For wheat, I’ll do what has worked on my land: sow in October, use a local good variety, put part of the fertilizer before sowing and add more at jointing. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll plant summer maize quickly on the same land, with simple tillage so I don’t miss the season. Maize doesn’t always need much water if summer rain comes, so I’ll watch the sky and only irrigate if it stays dry. Stevia I’ll keep on a smaller plot, use moderate fertilizer, and spend more time on weeding and field checking because that crop is more troublesome than grain. I am not chasing the highest yield. I want a year that is stable and does not leave me short of cash.
